subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through FintechCo's usage patterns and multi-tenant concerns. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have this captured in one place.

1) Key pain points you highlighted
- Noisy-tenant effect: a small set of customers generate large bursts and impact p99 latency for everyone.
- Lack of per-customer throttles and burst protection — leads to downstream queueing and dropped requests.
- Difficulty tiering by plan: enterprise accounts need higher throughput + routing guarantees.
- Auditability and per-tenant usage reporting for billing and compliance.

2) Current stack (as described)
- Primary model requests go to OpenAI-hosted endpoints via an in-house proxy.
- Proxy publishes inbound requests to Kafka for async processing/metrics; spikes are mitigated with a simple queue today.
- No isolation of KV caches or prefix caches per tenant; shared cache is contributing to noisy neighbors.

3) Success criteria you defined
- Per-tenant throttles that prevent noisy tenants from degrading others (target: keep p99 latency increases < 25% during 95th percentile bursts).
- Ability to define plan-based tiering: e.g., Standard vs. Enterprise (Enterprise gets dedicated routing/pinning and higher concurrent tokens).
- Per-tenant usage reporting to tie back to billing (daily granularity) + audit logs retained for 12 months.

4) Multi-tenancy controls we discussed (what FintechCo needs)
- Rate limits & quotas: per-second concurrency limits, token quotas (monthly), and burst allowances (token-burst or request-burst windows).
- Per-customer routing/policies: route high-tier customers to pinned capacity or priority queues; fallback to shared pool when capacity constrained.
- Tiering needs: support for plan-based configs (plans, custom overrides, per-tenant overrides), and easy promotion/demotion.
- KV/prefix cache isolation options or cache key namespacing to avoid cross-tenant pollution.

5) Immediate next steps
- Ben / Marissa: we will produce an initial config proposal + architecture sketch and cost delta by Tue 2026-07-20. (Attached: multi-tenancy-controls-ask-grid.csv + redwood-multi-tenant-arch.png)
- Marissa to book a technical deep dive to map FintechCo's traffic shapes to config recommendations — propose Jul 16 for that call.
- FintechCo: share a 24-48 hour sample of request/traffic shape (you mentioned an anonymized payload sample) — Alex / Priya to attach.

If I missed anything or any of the success criteria above needs tuning, please flag. We're happy to prioritize the deep-dive and put together a proof-of-concept config that enforces per-tenant rate limits + routing rules.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & next steps

Thanks Ben — this is great and captures the conversation. A few clarifications and additional items from our side:

- Confirm we need token-based monthly quotas (to match our billing) and a hard concurrency cap per-tenant. Burst policy should allow short spikes (seconds) but protect sustained spikes.
- Enterprise accounts (~12 customers) should have option to be pinned to dedicated capacity; otherwise they get priority routing into the shared pool.
- Compliance: SOC2/audit logs will be a blocker for procurement; can you confirm retention options and which events are included in the logs? We need at least 12 months of request/response metadata and config-change audit trails.

I've attached a small sample of our traffic for a representative 6-hour window (anonymized). File: fintechco-traffic-sample.json

We're available for the technical deep-dive on Jul 16 (10:00 AM PT) — please send a calendar invite. Also, would like a rough back-of-envelope on the cost delta for dedicated pinning vs. priority routing for our enterprise tier (ballpark monthly figures).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Platform Engineering
FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com

Attachments: fintechco-traffic-sample.json
